mainTopic: Whether replacements (חילופין) are like growths (גידולין), with two rejected proofs; then a new משנה on who is forbidden by a חרם vow and the exception for national property
overview: The גמרא finishes a two-sided question about the משנה's rule that replacements (חילופין) of forbidden fruit are forbidden. Either that is a special strictness for someone who forbade the fruit to himself, or replacements are treated like growths (גידולין), so the rule would apply to anyone. רב אחא בר מניומי brings a ברייתא to show that replacements are not like growths. In that case a wife under her husband's קונם borrows money, and her lenders collect from him. רבא rejects the proof: maybe replacements are forbidden לכתחילה, but once done, it stands בדיעבד. A second proof, from קידושין done with money from selling ערלה fruit, is rejected the same way. Then a new משנה begins. It teaches that the wording of a חרם vow decides who is forbidden to benefit from whom: the listener, the speaker, or both. Even when both are forbidden, both may still use property of עולי בבל, which belongs to the whole nation.

steps.title: The second side of the question: are replacements like growths?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its question. Maybe replacements are forbidden because חילופין are like גידולין. If so, the rule is the same whether a person forbade the fruit to himself or to his friend.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe the reason is that replacements are just like growths. If so, there is no difference between him and his friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a two-sided question about the משנה. Here it gives the second possible reason that replacements of forbidden fruit are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first side, said just before this, was that the strictness might apply only to someone who forbade fruit to himself. This second side says replacements are forbidden because they count like things that grow from the fruit. If that is the reason, the rule should apply equally when someone forbids fruit to his friend.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. Introduces the second side of a question
Replacements. Things received in exchange for the forbidden item
Growths. What grows out of the forbidden item, like plants from seeds
There is no difference

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new question. It is the second half of a question that started just before this. The words 'him' and 'his friend' mean a person who forbade the fruit to himself and a person who forbade it to his friend.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is because replacements
are considered like growths,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא הוּא וְלָא שְׁנָא חֲבֵרוֹ.
phrases.english: so there is no difference for him and no difference for his friend.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the person who made the fruit forbidden to himself. 'His friend' is when he made it forbidden to someone else.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא מִשּׁוּם דְּחִילּוּפִין כְּגִידּוּלִין דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question that began before this section
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are replacements forbidden because they are like growths? If so, the rule applies whether the fruit was forbidden to oneself or to a friend.

steps.title: Proof from a wife who borrows money and creditors collect from the husband
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר מניומי brings a ברייתא. A husband made benefit from himself a קונם for his wife. She may borrow money, and the lenders collect from him. He argues this works only if replacements are NOT like growths.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר מניומי said: Come and hear a proof. A man told his wife, 'Benefit from me is a קונם for you.' She may borrow money, and the lenders come and collect it from him. Why are the lenders allowed to collect? Isn't it because replacements are not like growths?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר מניומי tries to answer the question with a ברייתא. He tries to prove that replacements are NOT treated like growths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the husband pays her lenders, his money indirectly replaces what she received, so she benefits from him in a roundabout way. If replacements counted like growths, this should be forbidden. Since the ברייתא allows it, he concludes that replacements are not like growths.

keyTerms.meaning: A word used to make a נדר that forbids benefit
She borrows
Creditors, the lenders
They collect payment

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי, תָּא שְׁמַע:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Minyumi said: Come and hear:
One who says to his wife:
'Benefit from me is קונם for you,'
phrases.notes: The wording is a bit unusual, but the case is that the wife may not benefit from her husband.

phrases.english: she may borrow, and the creditors come and collect from him.
What is the reason the creditors may collect?
Is it not because replacements
are not considered like growths?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question in step 1
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a wife under a קונם who borrows, with her creditors collecting from her husband

steps.title: רבא: maybe it is only forbidden at the start, but valid after the fact
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof. Maybe replacements are forbidden לכתחילה, but once done, it is done. The ברייתא could be describing an after-the-fact situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Perhaps it is only forbidden from the start, but if one already did it, it is done.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes off רב אחא בר מניומי's proof. He shows the ברייתא does not prove that replacements are fully permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא suggests a middle position: replacements may be like growths and forbidden לכתחילה, but the action still stands בדיעבד. So the lenders collecting from the husband does not show that replacements are totally allowed. The question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, ahead of time, the ideal way
But if he did it, it is done. Valid after the fact (בדיעבד)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying replacements are permitted. He is saying they may still be forbidden לכתחילה, and the ברייתא only shows that the action stands once it has happened.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Perhaps it is only from the start that it is not allowed,
but if one did it, it is done.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: דִּילְמָא לְכַתְּחִילָּה הוּא דְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the wife's creditors
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may only show that the action works after the fact. It does not show that replacements are permitted from the start.

steps.title: Second proof: betrothal with money from selling ערלה fruit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה. Betrothal with ערלה fruit does not work, but betrothal with the money from selling them does work. This seems to show that replacements of forbidden items are not like the original.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, come and hear: One who betroths a woman with ערלה fruit, she is not betrothed. If he sold them and betrothed her with the money, she is betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first proof failed, the גמרא tries a new proof. It uses a משנה about קידושין done with ערלה fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערלה fruit is forbidden for benefit, so it has no value and cannot be used for קידושין. Yet the money received for selling it does work. That suggests the money, which is a replacement, is not forbidden like the fruit, so replacements are not like growths.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Moves on to a new attempt after the first one failed
One who betroths a woman (קידושין)
Fruit of a tree's first three years, forbidden for benefit
Their money, the price received for them

phrases.english: Rather, come and hear:
One who betroths with ערלה fruit, she is not betrothed.
If he sold them and betrothed with their money,
she is betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 3 rejected the first proof, a new proof is offered
steps.raayaObject: Replacements of a forbidden item are not like growths
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה in קידושין about betrothing with ערלה fruit or with the money from selling it

steps.title: Same rejection: only forbidden at the start, valid after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second proof the same way. Using the replacement money may be forbidden לכתחילה, but the קידושין still works בדיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too: it is only forbidden from the start, but if one already did it, it is done.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the ערלה proof using the same answer רבא gave before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קידושין working only shows that the act is valid after it was done. It does not show that one may use ערלה replacement money from the start. So the possibility that חילופין are like גידולין stays open, and neither proof settles the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too. Applies the same answer as before

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs that replacements are not like growths are rejected with one idea: something can be forbidden לכתחילה and still be valid בדיעבד. So the question of whether חילופין are like גידולין is still unresolved at this point.

phrases.english: Here too:
it is only from the start that it is not allowed,
but if one did it, it is done.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 4 using the reasoning from step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from ערלה money used for קידושין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The קידושין being valid only shows it works after the fact. It does not show that replacements are permitted from the start.

steps.title: Who is forbidden depends on how the vow is worded
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives three cases of a חרם vow. 'I am חרם to you' forbids the other person. 'You are חרם to me' forbids the one who made the vow. Saying both forbids both of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone says 'I am חרם to you,' the person the vow is aimed at is forbidden. If he says 'You are חרם to me,' the one who made the vow is forbidden. If he says 'I am to you and you are to me,' both are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It teaches that the wording of a חרם vow decides which person is forbidden to benefit from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whoever is called 'חרם' becomes like Temple property, and the other person may not benefit from him. So 'I am חרם to you' makes the speaker's things forbidden to the listener. 'You are חרם to me' makes the listener's things forbidden to the speaker. Saying both works in both directions at once.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; it marks the start of a new משנה
Something dedicated to the Temple, which no one may benefit from
The person the vow is aimed at, who is forbidden by it
The person who made the vow

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the person who made the vow is always the one forbidden. In 'I am חרם to you,' the one making the vow is not forbidden at all. It is the other person who may not benefit from him.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If one says: "I am hereby forbidden to you like חרם":
phrases.notes: In other words, 'treat me like Temple property, so you can't benefit from me.'

phrases.english: the one the vow is aimed at is forbidden.
If one says: "You are hereby forbidden to me like חרם":
the one who made the vow is forbidden.
If one says: "I am forbidden to you and you are forbidden to me":
both of them are forbidden,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא's discussion of replacements (חילופין) ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The person called 'חרם' becomes forbidden for the other to benefit from. Whoever is the 'other' side is the one who is forbidden, and if both are called חרם, both are forbidden.

steps.title: Both may still use property of the whole nation
steps.stepSummary: Even when both people are forbidden to each other, each may still benefit from things that belong to all the Jewish people, called 'property of עולי בבל.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But both of them are permitted to use things that belong to those who came up from Babylonia.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a limit to the vow. Things that belong to the whole nation are not forbidden, even to two people who vowed against each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: National property, such as things set up by the Jews who returned from Babylonia, does not belong to any one person. So neither person is benefiting from the other's property when he uses it. The vow only covers what belongs to the person called חרם.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jews who came up from Babylonia to the Land of Israel. Their property belongs to the whole nation.
Permitted
Both of them

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: a vow against benefit only covers what a person truly owns. Property that belongs to everyone is not counted as any one person's share.

phrases.english: and both of them are permitted
in things belonging to those who came up from Babylonia,
phrases.notes: This means things owned by the whole Jewish people together, so no single person owns them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מוּתָּרִין בְּדָבָר שֶׁל עוֹלֵי בָּבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the third case of step 6: even when both are forbidden, national property stays permitted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Property belonging to the whole nation (עולי בבל) is permitted even to two people forbidden to each other by a חרם vow.
